take_homes: The model re-reads the whole conversation each time, so what I put in first steers the result. I can write it once in a rules file.
The agent grades its own work too kindly, so its report is a claim that someone with domain knowledge has to check.
The licence is not the whole value. A rules file that carries over between sessions is something the organisation owns.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent and a short rules file, and have the controller check every figure against the ledger.
monday.when: Next month-end close, if IT allows it. Otherwise nothing happens.
monday.stop_condition: Any figure that doesn't match the ledger, or review time that doesn't drop against last month.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and nobody here has said what the monthly cost per user is.

misconception.why: It said the tool didn't improve and the user's context and rules did. That means a licence alone doesn't deliver the result. I still don't see how the organisation builds this, and I still don't know the cost.

one_line: Two good points, check the agent's report and write your rules once, but they came wrapped in a personal website, with no cost or payback anywhere.
